content.question_text: What does the "is-a" rule state regarding inheritance?

core_requirements: Every object of the subclass is an object of the superclass.
acceptable_variations: Every manager is an employee, but the opposite is not true.

content.question_text: How does the substitution principle formulate the "is-a" rule?

core_requirements: You can use a subclass object whenever the program expects a superclass object.
acceptable_variations: A subclass can be substituted anywhere a superclass is expected.

content.question_text: What does it mean that object variables are polymorphic in Java?

core_requirements: A variable of a specific type can refer to an object of that exact type, or to an object of any of its subclasses.
acceptable_variations: An Employee variable can hold an Employee object or a Manager object.

content.question_text: If you assign a Manager object to an Employee variable, can you call Manager-specific methods (like setBonus) on that variable? Explain why.

core_requirements: The compiler only considers the declared type of the variable (Employee), which does not have the subclass-specific methods.
acceptable_variations: No, because the compiler considers it to be only an Employee object based on its variable declaration.

content.question_text: Is it legal to assign a superclass reference to a subclass variable (e.g., Manager m = staff[i])? Explain why.

core_requirements: Not all objects of the superclass belong to the subclass (e.g., not all employees are managers).
acceptable_variations: No, because it could cause a runtime error if the object isn't actually of the subclass type.

content.question_text: What happens at runtime if you alias a Manager array as an Employee array and attempt to store a plain Employee object into it?

acceptable_variations: The program throws an ArrayStoreException because it tries to put an incompatible type into the underlying Manager array.

content.question_text: How do arrays in Java prevent the corruption of storing incompatible references into an array that was aliased to a superclass type?

core_requirements: All arrays remember the element type with which they were originally created.
They actively monitor that only compatible references are stored into them.
acceptable_variations: Arrays know their creation type and check compatibility at runtime to prevent memory corruption.
